newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BUBA rate cut 'not likely' in short term - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: BUBA rate cut 'not likely' in short term - Tietmeyer.

text.p: German Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said in an interview recorded on Monday and to be broadcast in Hungary next week that a fall in the German central bank's interest rates was unlikely in the short term.

"We shall follow very carefully the monetary figures which for the time being are too expansionist and therefore in the short term a further fall in interest rates is not likely," he told Hungarian radio.

"The monetary conditions for growth are given because the interest rates are lower than ever before. We have the central bank interest rates at a record low, we have the capital market interest rates also at a record low, so on the monetary side the preconditions are given for new growth."

Tietmeyer was speaking in an interview given to Hungarian radio in Franfurt on Monday which is to be broadcast to coincide with the arrival in Hungary next Tuesday of German president Roman Herzog for a three-day visit.
